title: Both inclinations (Mishnah Berakhot 9:5)
hook: bless for the bad as for the good, and love God with both your inclinations
tomorrow: a dream you never think about again: is it a letter unopened?

segments.voice: Yesterday, bless the place: Rava sent a man back to bless the road where the lion came at him. Today, a blessing for the lion itself, the bad thing.

Gratitude posts go up for the promotion and the acceptance letter. Nobody posts thankful for the layoff. The Mishnah does something stranger. It says a person must bless for the bad just as for the good. And it proves it from a word that looks misspelled. So why would heart be spelled with an extra letter?
screen: `THANKFUL FOR THE PROMOTION.` → `BLESS FOR THE BAD, TOO.` → `A WORD WITH AN EXTRA LETTER.`

segments.voice: The verse is the one recited in the Shema: "And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might." The ordinary Hebrew word for heart is lev. But here the Torah writes levav, with the letter bet twice. One classic explanation: a doubled letter, a doubled heart. So the Mishnah reads it: with all your heart means with both your inclinations, the good one and the bad one. The pull toward kindness, and the pull toward wanting, grabbing, sulking, all of it can love God. Then it keeps going. With all your soul: even if your life is taken. With all your might: and here it plays on the sound, for whatever measure is measured out to you, give thanks. That's the root of blessing the bad. Elsewhere the same chapter gives the words for bad news: blessed is the true Judge. Here's what a skimmer would miss. Blessing the bad isn't pretending it's good. Bad news gets its own blessing, not the good-news one. The Mishnah doesn't ask anyone to fake a feeling. It asks for the whole heart, both halves, to stay turned toward God, even when the measure is hard.
screen: `LEV, OR LEVAV?` · `TWO LETTERS, TWO INCLINATIONS.` · `FOR EVERY MEASURE, THANKS.` · `NOT PRETENDING IT'S GOOD.` · then, large: `BLESS FOR THE BAD TOO.`

segments.voice: Name one hard thing out loud, plainly, without dressing it up. Then name one thing you still love with your whole heart. Let the two sit side by side for the rest of the time, neither one canceling the other.
screen: `ONE HARD THING, OUT LOUD.` · `ONE THING YOU LOVE.` · `SIDE BY SIDE.`

segments.voice: Both inclinations: the Mishnah's reading of levav, the doubled heart, the good pull and the bad, both able to love God.
Keep it near: bless for the bad too, without pretending it's good. Thirty-four of fifty.

howItsDone: Jews say a blessing on good news and a different one on bad news, 'blessed is the true Judge' (Baruch Dayan ha-Emet), which is also said on hearing of a death.

fork.setup: your best friend didn't get into the program she wanted. she says, "everyone keeps saying everything happens for a reason. i just want to be sad." what does the Mishnah offer?
options: let it be bad: the Mishnah has a blessing for bad news that doesn't pretend.
help her find the reason fast, since she should be thankful for everything.
change the subject: blessings are for good news, so leave God out of it.
fork.reveal: a person blesses for the bad as for the good, but with the bad news blessing: blessed is the true Judge. the whole heart, both halves, without faking a feeling.

original.note: Hebrew: your heart, in Deuteronomy 6:5, written with a doubled bet.

trapdoor: what you thought: be thankful for everything, even the bad.
what it means: bless for the bad with a blessing made for bad news, and love God with both inclinations.

what a scholar hears: Mishnah Berakhot 9:5 reads Deuteronomy 6:5's levav as both inclinations and me'odekha as 'for every measure (middah), give thanks (modeh)'; 9:2 gives 'the true Judge' for bad tidings.
guess: the good pull and the bad pull, both able to love God
two hearts at war, until the good one finally wins
a choice between the good path and the bad one
recall: bless where you were saved, every time

chat.says: school cut the showcase to ONE night. am i supposed to say a bracha for THIS??
options: The Mishnah says bless for the bad too, with its own blessing. No pretending it's good.
Only once you've found the good in it. Then it counts as a blessing.
No. Blessings are for good news. For this, you're allowed to skip God.
